title: GAIA: Glass-Aware I/O Middleware
problem: Quartz glass archival storage has hybrid mechanical-optical architecture (XY mechanical, Z optical) introducing unique performance bottlenecks that conventional I/O scheduling cannot address.
motivation: Glass storage offers multi-century durability and radiation resistance, requiring specialized middleware to unlock performance potential.
method: The system coordinates three strategies to handle the storage hardware's unique design. Zigzag Data Placement arranges data to align with the mechanical stage's side-to-side motion, reducing wasted movement. Z-Axis First Placement prioritizes the fast optical axis before slower mechanical movements. Shortest Moving Time First scheduling selects operations based on predicted movement time, processing those requiring the least motion first.
key_novelty: This is the first I/O middleware designed specifically for glass archival storage systems that combine mechanical and optical movement.
contributions: Zigzag data placement algorithm aligned to mechanical stage motion
Z-axis-first placement strategy for optical traversal optimization
SMTF scheduling based on movement time prediction
82% read latency reduction vs traditional schedulers

metrics.other: 82% read latency reduction vs baseline schedulers

limitations: Glass-storage specific; write latency not addressed; evaluation on enterprise workloads and various glass sizes.
primary_theme: Middleware for hybrid glass storage optimization
